subject: [Bugfix][GDN] Fix stateless first-chunk classification (#51565)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51562.

`GDNMetadataBuilder.build()` passed `decode_threshold=1` to
`split_decodes_and_prefills()` while leaving
`treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`. As a result, every one-token sequence was
classified as a decode, including the first chunk of a request with no prior GDN
state. The decode path then reads recurrent and convolution state unconditionally;
because Mamba-style state pages can be reused without being zeroed, that first token
could consume stale state from a previous request.

This change:

- classifies non-speculative one-token chunks from state availability
  (`seq_len <= query_len`) and the runner's `is_prefilling` signal;
- keeps resumed one-token chunks and CUDA graph capture dummy batches on the decode
  path;
- stages FULL CUDA graph metadata based on graph-compatible shape rather than the
  derived prefill/decode split, so mixed and all-stateless batches use persistent
  buffers correctly; and
- adds regression coverage for stateless first chunks, resumed one-token chunks,
  capture dummy metadata, and CUDA graph staging.

The fix lives in the shared GDN metadata builder and therefore covers its Qwen,
OLMo, InternS2, Bailing, and standalone Kimi-Linear users. Runner-level FULL CUDA
graph selection is a separate concern tracked by #47123; this PR does not duplicate
that broader runner change.

Duplicate-work check (2026-08-09): issue #51562 has no comments, and searches for
open PRs referencing `51562` or matching `GatedDeltaNet metadata stateless decode`
returned no results. Related PR #51483 changes the Kimi K3 subclass rather than this
shared builder.

AI assistance was used to inspect the issue, identify the root cause.  I reviewed the final diff and the test results below.The submitting author reviewed every changed line in the final diff.

## Test Plan

1. Run the GDN metadata builder unit tests.
2. Run Ruff lint and formatting checks on both changed files.
3. Before marking the PR ready, run an end-to-end affected-model evaluation with a
   freshly allocated/reused GDN state page and a one-token first chunk.

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new stateless-first-chunk  …[truncated]

subject: Fix/whisper xpu varlen encoder decoder (#36298)
pr_body:
## Motivation

Encoder Decoder models produces garbage output on the intel_xpu backend (page_size > 1). Two root causes in the paged encoder-decoder KV path:

1. Cross-attention page table not converted to page numbers. encoder_page_table was left token-granular while the paged kernel interprets its entries as page indices — the decoder attended to wrong encoder KV.
2. Decoder KV region not page-aligned. e.g. whisper reserves max_source_positions (1500) encoder slots, but 1500 % page_size ≠ 0, so the decoder KV started mid-page. The paged decode kernel/allocator assume each sequence begins on a page boundary (physical slot = page * page_size + i % page_size), so decoder tokens were read/written at wrong slots.

## Modifications
- Modified `xpu_backend.py` to route cross- and decoder self-attention in encoder decoder model to `flash_attn_with_kvcache` with page_size=1 support added in https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/454

subject: [Bugfix] Fix mHC block-M prenorm GEMM cross-row reduction carry-over (#49429)
pr_body:
In hc_prenorm_gemm_block_m_tilelang, T.alloc_var(init=0.0) declared inside the unrolled i_m loop is hoisted and initialized only once, so the cross-warp reduction accumulator carries over between the rows of a block: every odd output row (and its sqrsum) is the sum of both rows in its block. The block-M kernel is selected for num_tokens >= 1024, so DeepSeek-V4 mHC prefill produces corrupted mixes for odd tokens whenever the DeepGEMM path is not in use. Use per-row locals instead.

Verified on B200: odd-row output equaled ref(even)+ref(odd) exactly and odd-row sqrsum was 2x before the fix; all
tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py cases pass after (including the previously failing num_tokens=2048 parametrizations).

subject: Fix attention backends for models with per-layer head counts (num_attention_heads_per_layer) (#32625)
pr_body:
## Motivation

Both attention backends assume a uniform query head count across layers. Models that set `num_attention_heads_per_layer` (e.g. `poolside/Laguna-S-2.1`, 48–72 heads) break:

- **FlashInfer**: the prefill/decode indices updaters plan wrappers with the config-level `num_attention_heads` (48). `run()` silently accepts a 72-head q but only covers the planned work partition — output rows past ~qo·(48/72) of every prefill batch are corrupted on each >48-head layer (silent quality degradation).
- **Triton**: decode buffers (`attn_logits`, `attn_lse`) are sized with the config-level count while kernels index `layer.tp_q_head_num` → OOB writes → IMA / device asserts / CUBLAS failures.

## Modifications

Add `ModelConfig.get_max_num_attention_heads()` (max of `num_attention_heads_per_layer`, falling back to `num_attention_heads`) and use it at the four sizing/planning sites (FlashInfer prefill + decode updaters, Triton main + draft backends). Over-planning for smaller-head layers is safe: standalone `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` with plan=72/run=48 heads matches reference within bf16 noise.

## Accuracy Tests

`poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4` (48–72 heads/layer), 1x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP=1:

- Needle retrieval at 15k/40k/73k-token prompts: FlashInfer 1/3, 0/3, 2/3 → **3/3 everywhere**; Triton crash → **3/3 everywhere** (matches vLLM).
- Few-shot GSM8K 200q, FlashInfer: 0.33–0.35 accuracy / up to 0.245 invalid before → **0.64–0.71 / 0.000 invalid** after (Triton reference on the same stack: 0.79–0.83).
- No-regression check for uniform-head models: teacher-forced prompt logprobs (~15k tokens), stock vs patched, `google/gemma-4-12B-it` (Triton) and `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` (FlashInfer): **byte-exact, max |Δ| = 0**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — for uniform-head models the computed values are unchanged; for per-layer-head models buffers/plans grow to the per-layer max (required for correctness).

subject: [Bugfix] detect alibi and revert to FA2 (#15231)
pr_body:
On Hopper, Flash Attention 3 is enabled by default (since the v0.7.0 release), but FA3 does not support ALiBi positional encodings. This PR will revert to FA2 if alibi_slopes are passed in to `FlashAttentionBackend`.

In the v0.8.1 release, the error when attempting to use a model with FA3 with ALiBi (such as [bigscience/bloom-1b1](https://huggingface.co/bigscience/bloom-1b1)) is:
```
RuntimeError: If cu_seqlens_k is passed in, then page table is not supported
```

Now there is [change in vllm_flash_attn](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/50/files#diff-30bbb250b1fdc0d0d0ada8e34377e835bbb92f4b48ca42807fe10524fe5a3730R199) that will raise an AssertionError if alibi is used with FA3. This improves the error message, but the server would still fail to come up. With this PR, vLLM will fall back to FA2 instead of erroring.

FIX #13810

subject: [Bugfix] Restore moe_forward output shape invariant on TRTLLM MXFP4 path (#41646)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #41645. `gpt-oss-{20b,120b}` crashes under `torch.compile` with `tensor_parallel_size > 1` on Blackwell because of a fake/real shape mismatch in `vllm.moe_forward`:

- The TRT-LLM MXFP4 experts kernel (`TrtLlmMxfp4Experts{Monolithic,Modular}.apply`) writes output at `moe_config.hidden_dim_unpadded` (gpt-oss: 2880).
- The fake `_moe_forward_fake` returned `torch.empty_like(hidden_states)` whose last dim is the padded `hidden_dim` (gpt-oss: 3072 after the kernel-alignment pad in `_maybe_pad_hidden_states`).

When inductor's `assert_size_stride` checks the runtime tensor against the traced fake, it fires:

```
AssertionError: expected size 256==256, stride 2880==3072 at dim=0;
                expected size 2880==3072, stride 1==1 at dim=1
Error in op: torch.ops.vllm.moe_forward.default
```

The divergence was introduced by #40960 (added kernel-alignment padding without updating the fake).

## Approach

### `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py`

Add `hidden_dim_unpadded: int` to the `_moe_forward` / `_moe_forward_shared` (and matching fake) signatures. The caller in `MoERunner.forward` computes the value via `_trtllm_mxfp4_unpadded_dim`: returns `moe_config.hidden_dim_unpadded` only when the active backend is `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`, else 0. The fake allocates the narrow shape when the int is positive, else falls through to `empty_like(hidden_states)`.

Computing the discriminator caller-side rather than peeking layer state in the fake is necessary: doing the isinstance check inside `_moe_forward_fake` specializes the fake per-`layer_name` and breaks `torch.compile` subgraph dedup (`tests/compile/h100/test_startup.py::test_moe_startup` is the canary that catches this). `moe_config.hidden_dim_unpadded` alone is also insufficient: it encodes the model's logical hidden, not whether the active kernel narrows. Cutlass MXFP4 MXFP8 writes the full padded width and would be mis-classified.

subject: [AMD] Fix GPT-OSS MXFP4 accuracy on ROCm AITER path (#26884)
pr_body:
CO-OWNER: @bingxche 

## Motivation

On ROCm AITER, the GPT-OSS MXFP4 fused-MoE path was producing silently wrong outputs. With these server flags on MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache --port 8000
```

the AITER dispatcher was selecting `module_moe_ck2stages_b16_fp4x2_preshuffle_off_b16_swiglu_per_1x32_mulWeightStage2`, a `preshuffle_off` codegen kernel. But the weights had already been preshuffled by `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, so the kernel interpreted shuffled bytes as un-shuffled and the model emitted nonsense. lm_eval gsm8k `flexible-extract` dropped from ~0.88 to ~0.21.

There were two root causes:

1. **Wrong shuffle layout.** The old path used `shuffle_weight_a16w4(..., 16, True)` / `shuffle_scale_a16w4(...)`, which produce the **gate/up-interleaved** tile layout (`is_guinterleave=True`). The AITER MXFP4 fused-MoE kernels tuned for GPT-OSS — both the FlyDSL `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` entries in `gptoss_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` (which have `gate_mode="separated"`) and the CK `module_moe_ck2stages_*_preshuffle_on_*` fallback — expect the **separated** (`is_guinterleave=False`) layout, identical to what ATOM uses on the same hardware.

2. **`is_shuffled` flag never set.** `shuffle_weight_a16w4` returns a tensor with `.is_shuffled=True`, but the call site did `layer.w13_weight.data = shuffle_weight_a16w4(...)`. Assigning to `.data` does not copy custom Python attributes, so `layer.w13_weight.is_shuffled` stayed unset. `aiter.fused_moe` reads this via `getattr(w1, "is_shuffled", False)` and, seeing `False`, dispatches the `preshuffle_off` codegen — which assumes the weight bytes are *not* shuffled. With actually-shuffled bytes, this gives garbage output.

The two bugs interact: even if the layout had been correct, the missing `is_shuffled` flag would still have routed to the wrong codegen branch.

## Modifications

subject: [ROCm] Fix fused_moe_fake signature mismatch and other AITER bugs (#36100)
pr_body:
## Summary

Fix a real logic bug and several related issues in ROCm AITER ops:

### Main bugfix: `_rocm_aiter_fused_moe_fake` signature mismatch

The fake/meta implementation for the `rocm_aiter_fused_moe` custom op was missing 4 parameters (`hidden_pad`, `intermediate_pad`, `bias1`, `bias2`) that the real implementation has. Since `direct_register_custom_op` derives the op schema from the impl's signature, callers can pass these arguments to the op. In `torch.compile` / FakeTensor mode, PyTorch calls the fake with the same arguments, causing a **TypeError crash** because the fake doesn't accept them.

This is actively triggered by the MXFP4 CK backend code path in `mxfp4.py` (line 1162-1177) which calls:
```python
rocm_aiter_ops.fused_moe(
    ...,
    hidden_pad=self.hidden_pad // 128 * 128,
    intermediate_pad=self.intermediate_pad // 64 * 64 * 2,
    bias1=layer.w13_bias,
    bias2=layer.w2_bias,
)
```

### Other fixes
- Fix copy-paste error messages in `AiterFlashAttentionImpl` that incorrectly referenced `FlashAttentionImpl` (2 instances)
- Fix wrong KV cache layout comment: `[num_blocks, num_heads, page_size, head_dim]` -> `[num_blocks, page_size, num_heads, head_dim]` to match actual indexing
- Fix wrong variable label `use_mxfp4_aiter_moe` -> `use_rocm_aiter_moe` in QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod log message
- Fix method name typo `triton_fp4_gemm_dynamic_qaunt` -> `triton_fp4_gemm_dynamic_quant`
- Fix typo `deocde` -> `decode`, grammar `only support` -> `only supports`

subject: [BugFix] [Kernel] Fix GPU SEGV occuring in fused_moe kernel (#10385)
pr_body:
When running a large model (~500G), I encountered GPU SEGV. It was occurring in `fused_moe_kernel`:

```
Thread 98 "python" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
Warning: precise memory violation signal reporting is not enabled, reported
location may not be accurate.  See "show amdgpu precise-memory".
[Switching to thread 98, lane 0 (AMDGPU Lane 7:2:1:1/0 (0,0,0)[0,0,0])]
fused_moe_kernel () at fused_moe.py:142
142             b = tl.load(b_ptrs,
```
It seemed to me that this could be integer overflow. Changing offsets to use `tl.int64` in `fused_moe.py:fused_moe_kernel` fixes the issue.

subject: Fix the router GEMM inaccuracy when using _front_w in Kimi-K3 (#33764)
pr_body:
## Problem

The Kimi-K3 MoE layer computes the router logits in bf16. The router then
selects the experts from these bf16 logits. The selection is not accurate.

Other implementations use fp32 for this GEMM:

- vLLM sets `out_dtype=torch.float32` on its gate
- the SGLang EP front (`moe_front.fused_front`) uses `out_dtype=torch.float32`

Measurement with the layer-1 gate weight and the fp32 correction bias:

- 5.27% of the tokens get a different top-16 expert set
- 0.33% of the routed weight goes to different experts (mean); the p99 is 6.4%

Previously, as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29783 shows in GLM-5.2, this is not safe, and can drop the SWE-Bench Verified score by 79 -> 67. In fact since this path is gated by num_tokens, it will be really difficult to diagnose bugs in the future (when running evals quickly with large batch sizes, vs real world use at small batch sizes)

## The `_front_w` fusion

Three projections in the MoE layer read the same `hidden_states`:

| projection | weight shape at TP8 |
|---|---|
| `shared_experts.gate_up_proj` | `[1536, 7168]` |
| `gate` (the router) | `[896, 7168]` |
| `routed_expert_down_proj` | `[3584, 7168]` |

`_merge_front_weights()` concatenates the three weights along the row axis into
one tensor, `_front_w [6016, 7168]`. One GEMM then replaces three GEMMs. Each
module keeps a view of the merged tensor, so the memory does not increase.

```
hidden_states [M, 7168] --> _front_w [6016, 7168] --> fused [M, 6016]
                                                        |
      cols    0:1536  gate_up  --> SiTU --> shared down_proj
      cols 1536:2432  logits   --> router (sigmoid + bias + top-16)
      cols 2432:6016  latent   --> mxfp8 quant --> trtllm-gen MoE
```

The fusion saves 11-16 us for each MoE layer. The fusion also causes the problem. `fused` is one tensor, and one tensor has one dtype. Two of the three consumers need bf16 (SiTU, MXFP8 quant). Thus the router got bf16, which works functionally but not numerically correct.

## The fix

The GEMM writes fp32. The two other consumers read fp32 directly. No cast pass
and no new kernel are necessary.

subject: [XPU] Fix NemotronH (hybrid mamba2) launch on --device xpu (#32227)
pr_body:
## Motivation

Bringing up **NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B** (a hybrid Mamba-2 / attention model,
`NemotronHForCausalLM`) on `--device xpu` fails during server init with two separate,
sequential errors. Both are device/arch-coverage gaps rather than kernel bugs.

## Error 1 — `extra_buffer` mamba radix cache asserts out on XPU

With the default `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy auto`, the resolver selects
`extra_buffer` for supported hybrid archs (Nemotron qualifies). A device assertion
then rejects XPU:

```
File ".../server_args.py", line 5251, in _validate_mamba_extra_buffer
    is_cuda() or is_musa() or is_npu() or is_hip()
AssertionError: extra_buffer needs CUDA/MUSA/NPU/ROCm (FLA).
```

The `extra_buffer` path is FLA/Triton-backed and Triton has an XPU backend, but
`is_xpu()` was simply missing from the guard, so the strategy could never be used
on XPU even where it works.

## Error 2 — Triton backend indexes layer 0 as full-attention for a hybrid model

After clearing Error 1, init crashes selecting `v_head_dim`:

```
File ".../layers/attention/triton_backend.py", line 198, in __init__
    self.v_head_dim = model_runner.token_to_kv_pool.get_value_buffer(0).shape[-1]
File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 3649, in _transfer_full_attention_id
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: layer_id=0 not in full attention layers: dict_keys([5, 12, 19, 26, 33, 42])
```

`TritonAttnBackend.__init__` has a hybrid-model branch that avoids indexing layer 0
(which may be a Mamba layer, not full-attention), but it only tested
`hybrid_gdn_config` / `kimi_linear_config` / `linear_attn_model_spec`. **NemotronH is
detected by `mamba2_config`**, which is not in that set, so it fell through to the
`else` branch that assumes layer 0 is full-attention. Nemotron's full-attention
layers are `[5, 12, 19, 26, 33, 42]`, so `get_value_buffer(0)` raises. This affects
other `mamba2_config` archs too (FalconH1, Lfm2, ...), not just XPU.

## Modifications

1. **`server_args.py`** — add `is_xpu()` to the `extra_buffer` device guard (and to
   the assertion message).
2. **`triton_backend.py`** — replace the three-way hybrid check in the `v_head_dim`
   selection with the umbrella `mambaish_config( …[truncated]
